title: Diraq Expands U.S. Footprint with New Mexico Quantum R&D Laboratory to Advance DARPA QBI Milestones - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Silicon spin-qubit developer Diraq, a DARPA QBI Stage B contractor, signed an MOU to open an Albuquerque measurement R&D lab inside the Roadrunner Quantum Lab, funded with New Mexico matching money, while targeting 150,000 physical qubits per chip by 2029 and over 2 million by 2031.

insights.claim: Diraq targets 150,000 physical qubits per chip by 2029 and more than 2,000,000 physical qubits per chip by 2031 via monolithic integration on commercial 300mm silicon.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Very aggressive density targets; if met, silicon spin would leapfrog other modalities in qubit count.
insights.quote: 150,000 physical qubits / chip by 2029• >2,000,000 physical qubits / chip by 2031
insights.locator: Diraq Silicon Spin Qubit Hardware Roadmap

insights.claim: Using standard CMOS fabrication, Diraq aims for high-density qubit packing that bypasses footprint and interconnect bottlenecks facing non-semiconductor platforms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A key competitive argument for semiconductor-based qubits versus atoms, ions and photonics.
insights.quote: bypassing the footprint and interconnect bottlenecks that challenge non-semiconductor quantum platforms

insights.claim: Diraq is an active Stage B contractor in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, which involves independent technical audit toward DARPA's 2033 utility-scale quantum system goal.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QBI progression is an independent credibility signal for private quantum hardware companies.

insights.claim: New Mexico's $450 million quantum allocation provides state matching funds that will directly finance Diraq's cryogenic testing infrastructure at RQL, including Maybell Quantum dilution refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: State subsidies are attracting foreign quantum firms into the U.S., with Maybell as a supplier beneficiary.

insights.claim: The Albuquerque lab will begin operational bring-up by end of 2026 and complements Diraq's Palo Alto, Chicago and Los Angeles sites and Sydney R&D headquarters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Growing U.S. presence positions the Australian company for U.S. government work.
